messages.subject: JGR launcher
messages.body_plain:
Dear Sirs,
I am posting this question to you by sugestion of Markus Helbig.

I am user of JGR on ubuntu platform, where it has always worked fine. 
However, recently I installed R and JGR on ubuntu 14.04.2 but I was not 
able to create a shortcut directly to JGR.

I started R and run JGR() once, but the script (file "run") is not 
created (at least it is not in the expected folder).
Indeed, the only file at /usr/local/lib/R/site-library/JGR/scripts/ is 
run.in (run is absent).

I would acknowledge if you can give me a solution to this problem or an 
alternative way to create a launcher directly to JGR (rather than 
starting it from R).
Thank you in advance.

Yours faithfully

-- 
Dr. Juan Cesar Vilardi
Depto Ecologia, Genetica y Evolucion
Fac. Ciencias Exactas y Naturales
Universidad de Buenos Aires
1428 Buenos Aires-Argentina

messages.subject: Rserve: "ignoring SIGPIPE signal" returned while eval (bioconductor - xcms - packages)
messages.subject_clean: Rserve: "ignoring SIGPIPE signal" returned while eval (bioconductor - xcms - packages)
messages.body_plain:
Hello,
I'm currently struggling with that kind of errors (returning from R through Rserve):

Error : ignoring SIGPIPE signal


This usually occurs when a master instance of Rserve has just been forked and the forked instance has been asked to load some packages, or later while using some of its functions. This results in not loading the package, of course, or failing while trying to eval.

My web searches lead me to a related comment in Rserve source code:

#ifndef WIN32

    /* windows uses this in init, unix doesn't so we set it here */

    R_Interactive = Rsrv_interactive;

    /* we let R install sig handlers, but remove those that are bad */

    signal(SIGSEGV, SIG_DFL);

    signal(SIGILL, SIG_DFL);

#ifdef SIGBUS

    signal(SIGBUS, SIG_DFL);

#endif

    /* FIXME: not sure about SIGPIPE - it's ok to use R's handling when

       caused by R code, but it's unclear if it can be caused by

       Rserve's internal code which would prefer death to surrender ... */

#endif


So I suppose this is a matter Rserve dev has thought about while developing Rserve.

Notes:
1/ I'm working under Linux/Debian
2/ Using the java client
3/ The packages I am trying to load have dependencies (and come from "BioConductor")

I suspect this is all about doing the things at the right time (race conditions), but I'm not sure (never had that kind of issue before).
Thing is, I am well connected to Rserve, and it works fine (the very first thing I ask to the forked instance is to display R's version and some other very simple things).

Do you have any idea about that?
Any help would be greatly appreciated. Thanks by advance. 
The packages that won't work seem to depend on the "parallel" package or so (actually packages related to BioConductor like CAMERA, xcms, ...). And I read somewhere that R, in this kind of situation (parallel processing) get's a separate R environment for each core it plans to use. I also know that Rserve, in my configuration (Rserve running localhost), is not allowed/able to work on several environments (only the global one - .GlobalEnv).
Well, what is your opinion about all this. If I'm thinking right, is there any possible workaround? Have you ever tried to use the parallel package over Rserve running on localhost? Is there a chance that this is all about something else?

Thanks very very much again for your time.


Gauthier

messages.subject: Re: Rserve: "ignoring SIGPIPE signal" returned while eval (bioconductor - xcms - packages)
messages.subject_clean: Rserve: "ignoring SIGPIPE signal" returned while eval (bioconductor - xcms - packages)
messages.body_plain:
Gauthier,

SIGPIPE simply says that something in R tries to write to a file/socket which is already closed. R installs a handler on this because it assumes that you did this intentionally and thus you want to be informed - in most cases this aborts the corresponding R code that triggered this write.

So you’d have to figure out what you’re doing that causes this and whether you care. In the context of Rserve specifically, you may get this error if the client closes the connection to the session while the session is still generating output. In that case there is really nothing Rserve can do since the client is already gone - that’s what the comments below refer to but there is no action really since it’s inconsequential.

Cheers,
Simon

messages.body_plain:
Hello,
I've been running rJava on AWS m3.xlarge, c3.2xlarge and m1.large instances
using the Amazon EMR (AMI=3.6) types. They come with R 3.0.1 and I've
installed rJava (0.9.6).

When I call (i started R via R -d valgrind)

.jinit(parameters = c(getOption("java.parameters"), "-Xrs"))
.jaddClassPath(p1)

where p1 is here: https://sguha.pastebin.mozilla.org/8834483

I get a segfault.

ex amd64->IR: unhandled instruction bytes: 0x66 0xF 0x3A 0x61 0x4 0x46 0x19
0x72
vex amd64->IR:   REX=0 REX.W=0 REX.R=0 REX.X=0 REX.B=0
vex amd64->IR:   VEX=0 VEX.L=0 VEX.nVVVV=0x0 ESC=0F3A
vex amd64->IR:   PFX.66=1 PFX.F2=0 PFX.F3=0
==23206== valgrind: Unrecognised instruction at address 0x1658e33c.
==23206==    at 0x1658E33C: ???
==23206==    by 0xFFFFFFF6: ???
==23206==    by 0xDAFA07CF: ???
==23206==    by 0xDB07010F: ???
==23206==    by 0xDAF9FBBF: ???
==23206== Your program just tried to execute an instruction that Valgrind
==23206== did not recognise.  There are two possible reasons for this.
==23206== 1. Your program has a bug and erroneously jumped to a non-code
==23206==    location.  If you are running Memcheck and you just saw a
==23206==    warning about a bad jump, it's probably your program's fault.
==23206== 2. The instruction is legitimate but Valgrind doesn't handle it,
==23206==    i.e. it's Valgrind's fault.  If you think this is the case or
==23206==    you are not sure, please let us know and we'll try to fix it.
==23206== Either way, Valgrind will now raise a SIGILL signal which will
==23206== probably kill your program.

 *** caught illegal operation ***
address 0x1658e33c, cause 'illegal opcode'

Traceback:
 1: .External(interface, obj@jobj, returnSig, method, ...)
 2: .jcall(.rJava.class.loader, "V", "addClassPath", as.character(path))
 3: .jaddClassPath(p1)

Possible actions:
1: abort (with core dump, if enabled)
2: normal R exit
3: exit R without saving workspace
4: exit R saving workspace


Rather than attach a file, here is the url to
1. The text file containing the session commands and output -
http://people.mozilla.org/~sguha/m3.xlarge-on-emr-AMI-3.6.txt

2. The Rdata file containing the variable 'p1'
http://people.mozilla.org/~sguha/paths.Rdata

If you'd like the vgcore file (not sure if it'll help) i can share a
private link (it's ~ 1GB file)

messages.subject_clean: rJava crashes with -xrs on AWS Instances(m3.xlarge)
messages.body_plain:
Saptarshi,

generally, Java cannot be run inside valgrind, because is creates dynamic code which trips valgrind. Do you see any issues without valgrind? It works for me (/wo vg), but then it may depend on the actual existence of those paths. This is essentially just passed directly to Java code so I wouldn’t be surprised if this is something in the JVM rather than rJava.

Cheers,
Simon
